Any pair that shows containment refuses. The tests in host.rs cover an in-project root, .., a symlink onto an existing project, a not-yet component that still lexically lands inside, the project parent, a sibling name prefix, and a state dir nested in the project. A symlink whose target already exists inside the project is therefore refused. The function returns the non-canonical absolute root.

local_checks.invariant: The created checkout path is <root>/<repo basename>/<sanitized branch> and the branch directory cannot escape that parent.
local_checks.result: worktree_path uses Path::file_name and herdr_worktree_directory, which keeps only ASCII alphanumeric runs joined by '-'. SystemDispatchHost::create_worktree calls worktree_root before Rex git worktree add or Herdr --path. rex::create_worktree rejects an existing leaf via symlink_metadata, then create_dir_all on the parent and git worktree add of that path. A generated directory cannot contain a separator or '..'. create_dir_all follows a symlink already present at the configured root when that target is outside the project; the containment rule allows any outside directory, and the default root is <state>/worktrees under a directory fsperm requires to be a real 0700 directory.

local_checks.invariant: git worktree remove runs only for the recorded absolute path after it is distinct from the project root, listed by git worktree list for that project, and clean.
local_checks.result: system_inspect_cleanup canonicalizes the recorded path, rejects a non-absolute path and the project root via same_path, and requires the canonical path in git worktree list --porcelain. A missing directory converges without removal. Dirty status refuses before clean_planned_with_host. system_remove_git_worktree passes that same recorded path as one argv element after worktree remove, with no --force. Porcelain parsing only decides registration; it does not choose a different removal path. Windows removal renames the checkout aside only after those gates, and renames it back.

local_checks.invariant: follows_path_rule or a live Herdr checkout match must hold before a recorded worktree is removed.
local_checks.result: Rex always sets the match bit from follows_path_rule on the canonical path: non-empty sanitized branch directory, that file name, and parent name equal to the project file name, under any root. Herdr sets the bit from the open workspace's checkout path, and sets it true when that workspace id is absent. Standalone, which cli/clean.rs reaches via HostKind::detect outside Herdr and Rex, returns (false, true), and owned_elsewhere is false outside a host, so cleanup continues. In every case the path passed to git worktree remove is the recorded worktree string, not a path taken from git or Herdr output. A record that already names some other registered clean worktree is the stored selection of that checkout. The Rex-only name rule is stricter defense in depth for a rewritten record; it does not by itself select a different directory than the record names.

hardening: worktree_root returns the non-canonical absolute configured root. An existing symlink at that root whose target is already inside the project is refused; a symlink to some other existing directory is followed by create_dir_all and git worktree add. The default root stays under the private state directory.

Standalone cleanup and a Herdr cleanup whose workspace id is absent set target_matches without follows_path_rule. git worktree remove still receives only the recorded absolute path, and only when that path is not the project root, is listed for the project, and is clean. Rex applies the directory-name rule on every cleanup.

Values written by dispatch itself are a tsk/t<n> branch or a ref that already passed check-ref-format. A same-account edit of the record can place one leading-dash token in gh or ls-remote argv.

local_checks.invariant: A stored branch, base_ref, base_commit, or base_remote reused at cleanup, relaunch, or gh must not gain an extra git or gh option beyond the single stored token.
local_checks.result: Dispatch deserializes those fields as plain strings. Later git deletes and ancestry checks pass refs/heads/<branch> as one argument, so the branch text is not a separate option. delete_exact_tip's old value is rev-parse output of that ref; the PR deletion path uses it only when it equals gh headRefOid. update-ref is update-ref --no-deref -d <refs/heads/branch> <oid>. gh pr view and gh pr merge receive the raw stored branch as one argument, and merge_args hard-codes the method flag plus --match-head-commit. local_checks.invariant: A separator-free project token that matches two filesystem-distinct basenames is refused, and equivalent aliases collapse to one stored spelling.
local_checks.result: resolve_project_path collects stored task paths, archived project keys, and the invocation default and this_repo. basename_matches keeps only the last component, folds ASCII case, and drops paths_equivalent duplicates before sorting. One match returns the stored spelling; zero is Unknown; two or more is Ambiguous. Relative tokens and missing directories are NoDirectory, so they are not treated as basenames. tsk add, plan import, and quick-add !p all call this function, so a refused token creates no task.

local_checks.invariant: list -p and project archive, which use the permissive resolver, still refuse two distinct absolute namesakes and do not write on that error.
local_checks.result: resolve_permissive_project_path returns Ambiguous for two absolute paths that share a basename and are not the same directory. The exact stored-string short-circuit applies only when the token itself is a stored scope with no separator, which keeps a legacy bare scope addressable and does not choose between two absolute paths. Slash tokens stay literal rather than being reparsed as a second basename. list and archive turn Ambiguous into a refusal; archive returns changed false, so no project record is written. status and clean are not on this path.

local_checks.invariant: Task status and cleanup cannot select a repository from a bare project token.
local_checks.result: Both commands take a TaskAddress and look up one task by number or id. Neither calls resolve_project_path or resolve_permissive_project_path, so a basename collision cannot redirect them.

hardening: Permissive resolution returns an exact stored bare scope such as atlas before basename ambiguity, which is the tested legacy-scope rule. The strict resolver still returns Ambiguous for that pair, and two absolute namesakes stay Ambiguous on the permissive path.

local_checks.invariant: The binary path and key text written into tsk.lua cannot break out of a Lua short string.
local_checks.result: lua_string quotes the value, escapes quotes and backslashes, and writes every byte below 0x20 and DEL as a three-digit decimal escape, so a following digit is not consumed by Lua's \ddd rule. The installed binary path, unbind keys, and bind keys are all passed through it. parse_key rejects empty chords and any whitespace, control, quote, or backslash before a key is stored. rex.lua uses TSK_BIN only as an argv element. Rex config check runs on the staged file before rename, and a rejected merged config is written back from the previous bytes.

local_checks.invariant: The managed tsk.lua rename stays on one directory descriptor and cannot be steered through a symlink or a multi-component name.
local_checks.result: Unix Dir::open and openat use O_NOFOLLOW, new files use O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW and must be regular files, and renameat/unlinkat take a single component from the directory fd. name() rejects '.', '..', extra components, and NUL. validate() compares the path inode with the opened directory before commit. resolve_config follows a user config symlink only to choose the real file, then opens that directory no-follow so the link is not replaced. On Windows, tsk setup rex returns before any write.
